summary: Plutarch (about 100 CE) on Solon's Egyptian studies, the unfinished Atlantis poem and Plato's later treatment. The earliest surviving report on how Solon is said to have come by the story.

tree.title: Plutarch, Solon 26: Solon in Egypt with the priests of Heliopolis and Sais
tree.summary: Plutarch says Solon went to Egypt and studied with the priests Psenophis and Sonchis. From them, as Plato says, he heard the story of the lost Atlantis and tried to put it into Greek verse. The chapter then turns to his stay in Cyprus.

tree.title: Plutarch, Solon 31: Solon and Peisistratus, and the abandoned Atlantis poem
tree.summary: Mostly about Peisistratus's tyranny and Solon's later years. At 31.3 Plutarch says Solon began a great work on the Atlantis tale, learned from the priests of Sais, and dropped it, not for lack of leisure as Plato says, but from fear of the task in old age.

tree.title: Plutarch, Solon 32: Plato takes up the Atlantis theme; Solon's death
tree.summary: Plutarch compares Plato's Atlantis to a building site: Plato laid out great porches and courtyards, started late and died before finishing, so the tale is as unfinished as the Olympieion in Athens. The chapter then gives conflicting dates and stories about Solon's death.
